utterances.text: Your Honour, before my friend does that I would invite him to look at the second paragraph of the statement he gave on 14th November 1996 to Ms. Sabina Manke and the second paragraph clearly says: "I did not believe that I could add the entire and complete truth to the statements I gave to the Bosnian authorities." Clearly the questions of clarification sought by the Office of the Prosecutor were limited. I do not believe that counsel can now assert that only those matters which were dealt with there and then at that time represents the entire rectification of inaccuracies contained in these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think since Mr. Niemann and I neither one were there, we are going to have to leave it up to the witness to tell us that. I would like to ask one or two more questions, maybe I can clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You can ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, at the time you had your conversations with Sabina Manke regarding all these statements, one of the statements that you looked at and talked to her about was that one made on 15th January 1994, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think there was only one statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you think that statement was not one that she showed you on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think there was only one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The position you are taking here today then is that what was contained in that 15th January 1994 statement is not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To an extent. There is very little truth in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me move on to something else then, if I may. You told us yesterday how there was an occasion after you had been subjected to a beating when Mr. Mucic came into hangar 6 and approached you and talked to you directly, and asked you how you had received the injuries that were obvious to him. Do you recall that incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not tell him how you had received those injuries because you were afraid of the possible repercussions of telling him who had done it, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of that fear, you refused to tell him who it was that had assaulted you, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it that if you would not tell him who had assaulted you, then it would have been extremely difficult for him to identify and punish the person or persons who had done so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You certainly had the impression that he was legitimately trying to find out from you who had done that to you, so that he might be able to take some action regarding what had happened to you. That was certainly the way it appeared, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that at the time you were arrested, you had a 7.62 millimetre pistol in your possession.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a permit for that pistol?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that it was against the law for you to have that without a permit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have just one other matter that I would like to ask you about, I think. This is about the time after you were moved to Musala prison. Do you remember ever encountering a person by the name of Garo, a Croat who was drunk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us about that incident? What happened there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was about 8.00, I think it was winter, so it was already dark. Garo came, I really do not know his name, all I know is his nickname, Garo. He came with two or three of his policemen of the Croatian Defence Council. He entered the prison, he went amongst the guards and we just heard that there was something strange happening, that there was noise, and he told us all to go outside, to go to the hallway. We all went out, he came and brought four or five cardboard boxes of beer and he told us all to line up and take a beer. We all lined up and we took a beer each. Then an incident occurred between the authorities of the prison and Garo himself. They reached for their guns, we fled -- went back to our cells, and it more or less ended with no shooting, they did not shoot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did not Garo at one point --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the only time that I saw him. I never saw him again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he not at one point point a gun at your head?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he pointed the gun in my direction, but he did not intend to point the gun at my head, but somebody else's head, the head of a guard who was nearby, because a conflict had started with the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if any guards made efforts to get him removed from the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they all tried.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that one of those guards who was trying to get him out of the building was Mr. Landzo, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do remember that Mr. Landzo was present at that point, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. That is all I have. Wait a minute. (Pause). That is all I have, your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any other cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon. If it may please the court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may proceed, please. Cross-examined by MS. RESIDOVIC

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Kuljanin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My name is Edina Residovic, I am Defence counsel for Mr. Zejnil Delalic. However, before I start with my questions, same as my colleagues, I would like to ask you first of all that when I ask my questions that if possible your answers should be brief and precise and, second, if you do not understand the question please let me know immediately so that I could repeat the question. Third, something that my colleagues have not said and I wish to ask you that, is that you should understand that the two of us speak and understand the same language, and that others in this courtroom should follow our conversation. Therefore, I would like to ask you, when I finish my question you should wait so that on the headphones that the usher showed you, the headphones that are on the table, that you hear the English translation of my question and then give your answer after that. You do not need to put the headphones on, they will be on the desk in front of you and you will only hear the translation. Thus we would allow everybody to follow what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the day yesterday, you testified before this court that you were arrested and taken to Celebici together with your friend Miro Golubovic, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also know, Mr. Kuljanin, that Mr. Miro Golubovic testified before this court, is that correct? When my colleague the Prosecutor asked you about it --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, your Honour, we did not get an answer, I do not think. I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So at the beginning, there is a warning, when you hear the translation of my question, only then you should give the yes or no answer, because the interpreter cannot follow what we are talking about at the same speed. So when asked by the Prosecutor you responded that you had had a pistol; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If Miro Golubovic testified before this court that you had a sniper rifle and a pistol, was he then telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was telling the truth. The rifle was not mine. It was a small calibre rifle which was used for sport, for shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Mr. Kuljanin, you surrendered the small calibre rifle with sniper aiming equipment for sports shooting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not hand it over. It was not in my possession when I was arrested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the rifle was found at your place, as your rifle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, only the pistol was found in my possession. The rifle was on the other side of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if Miro Golubovic said that you had both the pistol and the rifle with sniper aiming equipment, then he did not give a true testimony before this court; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, this has been asked and answered. In addition to that, I object to questions which say that the witness is lying or not telling the truth. The witness should at least be given the benefit of the doubt and asked whether he was incorrect and then perhaps, depending on the answer, one can progress further than that. To ask this witness whether or not he is lying is an inappropriate question and I object to that form of question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I do apologise to my learned colleague. I did not use the verb "lie", I said that something was not the truth, or something was incorrect. I do not know about the translation my colleague received, and I think that I can ask questions -- ask the witness questions in accordance with the facts presented before this court. Mr. Kuljanin, did you know that Miro Golubovic also had weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if it is correct that Miro Golubovic had a machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Miro Golubovic's machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Has Miro Golubovic seen your small calibre rifle with sniper aiming equipment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when asked by the Prosecutor yesterday, you responded that you only had a pistol, you were not telling the whole truth; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The question was what I had in my possession at the time of the arrest, and I said that I had a pistol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore if the question asked was which weapons did you have, the precise answer would have been a 7.62 pistol and a small calibre rifle with sniper aiming equipment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also do know Nedeljko Draganic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Slightly, but I do know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If he also confirmed this fact before this court, the fact that you had a small calibre rifle with sniper aiming equipment, so that means that he did confirm the thing that you have just responded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the statement presented to the Prosecutor you had never mentioned equipment earlier; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the statement you gave to Ms. Manke you did not speak about your possession of weapons.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I did say that I had a pistol. I think that it is in the statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not tell her on that occasion either about a rifle with sniper aiming equipment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, you certainly know the person named Dragan Dragovic, nicknamed Drasko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us say that you would agree with me if I say that that is a person who is not very serious; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depends on who you are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He does not pay his debts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot really give you an assessment of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you gave Drasko Dragovic, you sold an automatic rifle to Drasko Dragovic for 300 Deutschmarks and he continued to owe you that money?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is not correct. If I had had that rifle I would have given it to him. He would not have had to pay for the rifle, because everybody had a rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just now you said that at the time, in Donje Selo, everybody had a rifle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in Donje Selo, in the Konjic municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the Konjic municipality, that means including Donje Selo, because Cerici, Bjelovcina and Donje Selo are part of the Konjic municipality; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, your father's name is Jefto, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your mother's name is Ljubica Cuca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your father used to worked in maintenance of railways; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he worked in Igman, in the military industry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So mill industry, I am asking you this because there are some other people named Milovan Kuljanin in this municipality, so we want to be certain that we can ask you questions about certain facts linked to the name of Milovan Kuljanin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just before the war you were convicted to four months imprisonment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was because of fighting and bodily harm; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but it was self-defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your younger brother is named Ranko and your elder brother is named Srecko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have a lot of aunts and uncles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were not in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the month of May they had already got to Borci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had fled, they did not go there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were members of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Srecko was the personal escort to the Colonel of the army of Republika Srpska named Risto Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not, I was in the prison at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he did tell you about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we do not talk to each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Mrs. Residovic, can we now start our break?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Is this part of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We will resume at 2.30. (1.00 pm) (Adjourned until 2.30 pm) 20 21 22 23 24 25 (2.30 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Please remind the witness he is still on his oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mrs. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mr. Kuljanin, we finished earlier by confirming that your brothers were both in the army of Republika Srpska but that you have not spoken to them about that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a dispute between you and your brothers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We do not live together.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I really do ask what the relevance of all of this is in relation to this witness. What does it matter if he is disputing with his brothers or not? Surely that cannot help the Chamber to come to any conclusion over the charges in this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: She is cross-examining. She may have her reasons for putting these questions. Yes, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mr. Kuljanin, you have also confirmed that you were arrested by Darko Verkic, together with the members of the military police of HVO and you were taken to Celebici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the war, Darko Verkic was an acquaintance of yours, even a friend.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this event you were rather disappointed and furious with Darko Verkic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You could say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You thought that he had deceived you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sometimes while you were in Musala, you used to say, due to that anger, that you would not regret dying, but before that you would like to take your revenge against Darko Verkic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not like to take my revenge on him, I would just like to pay him back, the same as he did to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, you said that your occupation was that of a waiter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that from January to mid March, you were a reservist of JNA in Mostar. Before joining the reservists you worked as a waiter at the railway station in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when asked by the Prosecutor, you said that before your reservist service, you said that you were with the regular JNA forces, you did not give a correct answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please, could you repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When asked by the Prosecutor about what your occupation was before you joined the reservists, you said yesterday that you had been in the regular JNA forces.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was in 1990 to 1991 and after I had served my national service, I did not do anything for six months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it is correct that immediately prior to joining the reserve forces in Mostar for a while you had worked as a waiter in Konjic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was before I had gone to the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In the reserve forces in Mostar with you there were ten or fifteen other persons from Konjic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a native of Konjic you knew that the SDS leadership which armed the Serbs carried most of the blame for what happened to part of the Serb population later; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think so, the SDS leadership was formed after all the other political parties, HDZ and SDA, had already been formed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the former JNA and the Serb forces continually shelled Konjic from the hills?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In which period of time?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From early May to be precise, from 4th May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 4th May, I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They thus inflicted evil against everyone, including the Serbs, if it is true that they were the ones who shelled.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If it is true that they had shelled then that is a correct assessment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, in your statement given to the representative of OTP, Ms. Sabina Manke, you said that for 40 minutes before you went for your first interview in front of the infirmary, you were badly beaten; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said, and you gave the date of two or three days after that, on 14th June, you were beaten so badly that you received 280 blows.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My colleagues at the hangar counted the hits. They listened to that. I did not count.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Kuljanin, that after the first 40 minutes of torture with different means, as you said, the investigators could have seen consequences of this abuse on you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course. They also have my medical records.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also, the consequences of those events of the 14th would also be visible plainly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question. On the 14th in 1992? Well I was examined five days ago, and it was visible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will be a bit more precise. In the statement given to the representative of OTP, Ms. Sabina Manke, you said that on 14th June you were beaten up, and that on that occasion you received about 280 blows. I am asking you now, were those injuries visible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that this statement that you gave after this mistreatment of 40 minutes was the first statement you had given at all, a statement given to any authority.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You confirmed to my colleague that after that you had given many other statements, both in writing and on video.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the prison itself, in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the assistance of the technical services I would like for the witness to be presented one of his statements. I have also provided the interpreters with a translation of this text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Which of the statements are you referring to, so that we might be able to assist?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is the statement from the month of June which this witness gave before video cameras, and when asked by my colleagues he did say that he had given those statements. Since this is a statement that shows the witness and what I am talking about, I want the witness to be presented -- I want this statement to be presented to the witness as a statement given outside the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I am not sure it is a statement which is identifiable here. If it is, the Registrar might be able to play it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I think this is exhibit 175.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a video statement, and I would like to ask the technical services to show it so that the witness could identify it and on the basis of that, for me to be able to ask questions. We have already confirmed the basis for showing it by the fact that the witness said that he had given this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: How do you identify the video so that the technical people can put it on the video section.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The video recording was submitted by the Defence to the technical services. Thank you. So can we now see the video recording, please? (Videotape played) "I want to address the public and to tell the truth about my stay in Mostar, and my stay in Konjic, where I am now. On this occasion I would like to address the former Yugoslav People's Army, the residents of Borci, that are biggest enemies of all the Serbian population in Konjic, that they have no mercy towards Serbs, Croats or Muslims. They only make troubles that you can imagine, that you can experience. I was in Mostar for about two months and I saw what that was, what kind of an army that was and where that was all going. These are only thieves, cheats and liars who came here only for the money and nothing more. They hope to have the borders of greater Serbia, and that is not normal. They are not aware that Serbia cannot be here. We do not need that. We need no Serbia here. I am personally convinced that at least 70 per cent of the citizens of Konjic want to live in Konjic. They want to live with Croats and Muslims as they have lived so far. They, well, those people in Borci put us in such a situation that we have to turn our backs on those with whom we used to sit in our homes and have coffee, because we are Serbs, because not all the Serbs are the same. Whoever is at Borci, these are extremists and nothing else. They should not fire those shells, they should think of all the people in Konjic. They should think of Muslims and Croats and of Serbs, but they do not think of anyone as far as I can see. There is no mercy. I want to say also that while I was in Mostar, where I was, that was one of the biggest mistakes of my life, that I had gone there, because I was unemployed, so we went, ten or fifteen of us, as far as I know, we just went there because the pay was good. Later, when I saw what that was all about, I fled back to Konjic. I am deeply convinced that the logic -- that the army in which I served, the former Yugoslav People's Army, that there is no logic for its being here. There is no need for that. They are just making our lives miserable, all of us. We would be the happiest, we, the Serbs, if they would leave this very minute from Borci and from Bosnia-Herzegovina as a whole. They have not brought any good to anyone in the whole of Yugoslavia, let alone to us here in Konjic. They climb up the hill and now they send their shells. These are not sane people. They are idiots, morons. I cannot -- I hate them so much that I cannot -- I would like to go up there now, if I only had something to burn them all. The biggest culprits after the army are the leaders of the SDS. Now none of them is here. They escaped a month ago. One cannot find them anywhere. They dragged the Serb people into an abyss and now they watch us from the distance of some 500 kilometres or even 2,000 kilometres. These are the people who fled abroad. These are the arms smugglers and war profiteers. They are paid to be Serbs. They were collecting money from the people and they did not ..." (Videotape stopped)

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kuljanin, did you recognise the person speaking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I spoke, but you cannot see the desk from which I was reading.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The statement was made after your first statement in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as I already said, you cannot see the desk from which I was reading.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Mostar with you, there were about ten or fifteen other persons from Konjic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you knew at the time that the town was being shelled from the eastern parts, from the direction of Borci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time, you were aware of the fact that the town was daily shelled from the direction of the Boracko Lake?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was what we were told.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since the witness identified this recording, I would like, in order to impeach the witness, I would like to tender this video recording as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What number is it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Defence exhibit D68/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kuljanin, you know that Witness N also testified here, we spoke about him yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also know that Witness N, together with you, was one of the reservists in Mostar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that he was there, but he was not there with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also know that in the reserve forces in Mostar, there were the following persons from Konjic there: (redacted), Milan Cecez, Mitar Manivada, Slobodan Cecez, Hristo Gligorevic, Mladen Zivak, Kuljanin nicknamed Corba, late, and another named Koprivica. Are those the ten to fifteen persons that you have spoken about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know three or four of them. I do not know the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us the name of the four, in addition to you and Mr. N?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. N, myself, Mitar Manivada, and Dusko Gligorevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You know Milan Cecez from Donje Selo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Slightly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that together with Lazar Cecez, he was responsible for arming the population of Donje Selo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that while in the reserve forces in Mostar, same as Milan Cecez, you received a salary amount of 200 Deutschmarks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember now, but thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct from Mostar, from the reserve forces, you fled on 10th March?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not flee, I had just come home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that at the time you took with you an automatic rifle and the pistol that we have spoken about here, and two bombs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I took a pistol and two bombs. I did not take the automatic rifle with me because it was widely available and I did not have any need to bring it with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in addition to the weapons that we have just talked about, you also had two grenades with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the examination-in-chief you said that you went to Donje Selo when the first shells started to fall on Konjic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said when the first -- when I started to feel unsafe in the town itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the fighting in Donje Selo, you often went to a cafe owned by Lazar and Grozdana Cecez; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is there that you heard an argument regarding the acquisition of 45 pieces of weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not hear the argument, there were some remarks and it was not 400 to 500 but 40 to 50 pieces of weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us if there was a comment regarding who should pay for this, for these pieces of weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this was not paid. One did not pay for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So all the weapons that were coming for the inhabitants of Donje Selo was free of charge for the inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. Maybe -- it is possible, but that is something that I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, you also know that in Donje Selo, in addition to automatic rifles and M47 rifles, there were also three -- there was an anti-aircraft machine-gun and a mortar launcher above Cerici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw one of those hand held rocket launchers. I do not know about two of them being there. There could have been ten but I saw only one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in hiding in Donje Selo, you know, you knew that Lazar Cecez spoke on the telephone with Borci; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not while I was in hiding. That was before the conflict. While we were in hiding we did not have a telephone, because the telephone lines were down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, my colleague showed you a statement which you had given in January while you were in Musala.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me if you know the name of Jasna Dzumhur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Judge Edina Bektasevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You gave one statement to Jasna Dzumhur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I may have, but I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Without anybody forcing you to do or say anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall giving that statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask for the witness to be shown again an identified statement from 12th January 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could I please see this statement because I do not have the statement amongst the documents in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The statement from 12th January was one of the statements presented by my colleague and the witness identified his handwriting. I could give you the statement again, if you have not identified it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, your Honour, I think they are looking for defendants' Exhibit 25/4. (Handed).

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On this statement you recognised the date and your signature.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So please, on the back side, could you see on the top of the page the signature of Jasna Dzumhur, do you remember now the circumstances in which you gave this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember seeing it, because I know Jasna Dzumhur personally, but I did not see her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not long ago you looked into the content of this statement and since when I asked you, you gave affirmative answers regarding all the facts presented there, could you please once again look at the statement and tell us exactly which fact in the statement is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I can have a moment. (Pause). There is quite a lot of truth in this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you recognise this statement as your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but it is not as an entire statement, it is more or less a reconstruction.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since the witness recognised the statement and identified it as his, I would like to tender this statement as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I object to that, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Let us hear the basis of your objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. These statements were taken when this man was held prisoner and the conditions under which he was operating at the time mitigate entirely against voluntariness and being a statement which was obtained, so far as his frame of mind is concerned, under conditions of duress. There is no objection to the statements that were not taken under those conditions, but in my submission, all of the statements taken whilst he was held prisoner under the conditions in which he has described, bearing in mind the fact that this Tribunal, in my submission, should not be seen to be admitting evidence obtained under these circumstances, having regard to the interest in the maintenance of human rights and having regard to the rules. It is my submission that it is inappropriate and contrary to the public interest that they be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, my client, as well as all the other persons in detention, are giving statements while in detention. The witness did confirm all the facts in this statement --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Except for some minor corrections because the statement is not a transcript, he confirmed his signature and we have seen him, we saw what he looked like at the time, so I believe if the Prosecutor can prove that the statement was given under duress does have the right to give such comments. The Defence in future will in addition to the Prosecution witness who confirmed that statements were not given with the use of force, he would bring other witnesses who would be heard. If duress is confirmed, the Defence, same as the Prosecution, in the light of Rule 95 has the right to suppress evidence. Therefore I am offering -- I am tendering this statement into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We seem to be reversing the onus of proof about voluntariness. You are the person tendering this statement, and it is on you to show it was voluntary. If he admits it was not taken voluntarily, you do not have to consider tendering it, because the rule is fairly clear on that. You are assuming that he is recognising his signature and the circumstances makes it voluntary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Is there a presumption that all statements made in detention are under duress?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honours. I am not sure there is any evidence being brought by the Defence that the guards at the UN detention centre at Scheveningen are regularly bashing up prisoners and dragging them around the place and subjecting them to all sorts of inhumane treatment, which if they were, would cast doubt on any statements the Defence wish to tender taken at that place, but nothing has been said of that so far, so it is only in relation to circumstances which these witnesses have attested to in the camps they were at the time. Your Honours, I raise no objection to the statement taken in Belgrade where the witness said he had an opportunity to examine it, he was not under duress, but there is overwhelming evidence, in my submission, about the conditions to which these people were being subjected and anything they say under those circumstances must be viewed in light of the conditions under which they were being subjected at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I think the statement was probably taken at Musala sports hall, and the evidence with regard to --

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I do not think it was a very comfortable place there either, your Honour. We have not led evidence because it is not relevant to these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: There is not very clear evidence that people were beaten up in Musala camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Because, your Honour, if we had led that evidence, the first objection would have been that it was irrelevant, because it is not relevant to the charges in this case, but I am certain we could lead a great deal of evidence about how unpleasant it was there. These people were being kept at that place, and particularly this particular witness was kept right up until 1994. One wonders what the charges were, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually to me, a lot of this argument is strange and new. I do not know any circumstance in which a statement is opposed on grounds of involuntariness, but the onus is shifted on the person who is opposing it to show that. I do not know about that anywhere. Whether a detention camp, whatever we call it, is a place perfectly convenient and congenial for taking statements of this nature should be satisfied by this person tendering it, to show that it was voluntarily done, and the person was perfectly free to make his statement. I think that is understandable anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might be able to help just a second? Regardless of whether the statement was taken under duress or not, once the duress is gone, if the person says, "Yes, I adopt that statement", then I should think it would be admissible, because any taint --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Do not assume that has been done in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, he said a few minutes ago that it was -- I think my notes say that as to that statement there is a lot of truth in it. As to others of these statements, he has said that he had a chance to look at them in the presence of an investigator from the Office of the Prosecutor, and he made whatever corrections he wanted to and so, your Honour, I think that could be easily viewed as adopting the statement, presuming we are not saying he is being coerced now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually, I am not arguing it for any side. It is for the parties who are presuming that the statement was either voluntary or by duress to prove the arguments they are putting forward. I am in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: What I am suggesting, your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I am relying entirely on the arguments proposed for its admissibility or rejection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: What I am suggesting, your Honour, is that it does not make any difference whether the original statement was voluntary if he voluntarily adopts the statement at some later date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Again we have Mr. Moran volunteering his views on this matter when counsel, Madam Residovic is already on her feet dealing with it. I fail to understand how Mr. Moran believes he has a right to speak on this matter at this stage. No doubt when he is confronted with an objection he can enlighten us on his views, but I feel at this stage that it is hardly appropriate, in my submission, to have two or three counsel jumping up and arguing these points. Nevertheless, your Honours, my submission is that there is no evidence that he has adopted this statement. He has already said that the person Jasna, the judge, whose name my notes are not clear on, it was not there so far as he is concerned. How can it be said he has adopted the statement? In my submission, your Honour, there is no evidence of that. He goes further, he says it is not an entire statement, it is more or less a reconstruction. My submission is that there is absolutely no evidence whatsoever that it has been adopted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we go back to the same thing several times. It is correct that we are discussing the conditions in the camp. It is true that many persons were detained because of possession of weapons and armed rebellion. It is also true that they were under investigation. Those are continuing issues that the Prosecutor is raising. The procedure was before the investigation commission in Celebici and before other relevant authorities of the Konjic municipality. Since the witness did say that in Musala, he did not give the statement under duress, that all the facts from the statement that could be read here before the court, he did recognise as facts which he claimed did happen, and that they are correct, I see no grounds for objection. As for the acceptance of this statement as part of the proceedings against this witness in Celebici, or later in the municipality of Konjic, so how else do we prove, your Honour, proceedings if Defence is unable to present each element of this procedure, and even when the witness recognises that everything he had said here may be a sentence or two different because this is not a transcript, as compared with his answers to my questions asked before this court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What was your question to him about the making of this statement? Did you put it to him that he made it freely and he had no coercion, no compulsion when he made this statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was the question, did he give the statement in Musala under duress, he said he did not, he said he recognised his signature and that he did know Jasna Dzumhur but that he could not remember if he gave the statement before her, because there are five signatures of persons who interviewed this witness on 12th January 1993. These were the answers of this witness. Before that, when asked by me, he confirmed all the facts contained in this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Absent involuntariness, then there might be only other factors that might make it inadmissible. If he has not put forward the fact that it was done involuntarily, then there are only other factors which might make it inadmissible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am having the transcript checked at the moment, but I have no record whatsoever that this witness was asked whether it was taken under duress or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, did you give this statement under duress or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was transferred on 9th December from Celebici to the sports hall in Musala, that was a prison. I, as well as all my other comrades, were never asked whether we wanted to give the statement or not. They simply came, they read out names from a list and they told us to give statements. I gave a statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion, did anybody force you to do anything, did anybody put pressure on you, did anybody beat you when you were giving this statement? I am not talking about the other statements.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not on that occasion, nobody hit me. They did not beat me, but they beat me mentally in other ways.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the statement was given voluntarily in the circumstances of the prison are the circumstances that you should decide about. The witness did confirm that he gave this statement voluntarily, that he signed it and he certainly was in Celebici and in Musala. That is an undisputed fact. Therefore, I am proposing that this statement be admitted as this witness's statement given in Musala in January 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness has said he was beaten mentally, which means that he was under such conditions of duress that the whole issue of voluntariness was beyond him because he was overborne by the circumstances to which he was subjected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If his own private fears or premonitions about what might happen to him, without anybody else making any appearance of subduing his concerns then perhaps that might be a consideration in favour of those persons who were questioning him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is not as extreme as having someone standing behind him with a baseball bat, but -- your Honour is laughing. I am not sure what your Honour finds amusing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I am very amused by this argument. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I was not aware I was being amusing. Your Honours, it seems to me that one has to have regard to the total circumstances under which these people were being detained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually, that might merely go to the weight of it. If he had volunteered his statement, then it might not matter what he had behind him for making the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I just ask the court to note that there can be no cloak of legitimacy put over the circumstances in which these people were being put, which is being suggested by Madam Residovic, absolutely no cloak of legitimacy, but I cannot take the matter any further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can go ahead. You can tender it. It depends on what weight one gives to such a statement. You might like to rely on it, but I do not know what meaning it has to anybody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: May I add something? You talk about my amusement, you said standing with a baseball bat behind the person who is making the statement. There is no such evidence and I am surprised that you gave that example.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: My understanding --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: There is no such evidence that while he was making that statement, someone was standing behind him with a baseball bat.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: There is a previous statement which was taken under those circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: -- taking a statement whether we should introduce it into evidence or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was saying it was not as serious as circumstances where someone was standing behind him with a baseball bat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It has not got to that stage. What he might have in mind is perhaps the earlier treatment he might have had meted to him. Whether it is a consistent pattern, after such a treatment where they go and take you and then you make a statement, there is no such evidence that a statement is made immediately after being beaten up, and then they take you and you make a statement, but in any event, when one is in the situation of incarceration, for certain proposals it depends on what the trial judge will make of such a situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: As your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, your Honour, I am tendering this statement as evidence for the Defence. Is that accepted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you give us a number for identification?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number is D25/4.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I do apologise, but is that Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document was submitted by Defence counsel for Mr. Landzo and that is why it bears the mark D25/4.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, in the statement you gave to Ms. Manke, representative of OTP, on page 2, you said that at the moment when you were taken out of the manhole, in addition to the persons you mentioned before this court, that Mr. Azinovic was also present, Mr. Ivica Azinovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see him, I think he was in the car. He was the driver of the van that transported me to building number 22. I am sure that Hazim Delic and Pavo Mucic were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that Ivica Azinovic was present and was watching while you were being beaten in front of the infirmary; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, several times, not once. He was the driver, as I already told you. He drove that IVECO van.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a few more questions. The fighting in Donje Selo took place between 20th and 23rd May; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so, but it was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were presented a statement which you had given before the court in Visegrad, and which you said you had no objections to, not while you were giving it nor later.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that that statement before the investigative judge in Visegrad was given within the process of giving statements for the Association of Detainees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The fact that you were giving a statement for the Association of Detainees --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I thought that this was for the court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the investigative judge, before you started giving your statement, did the judge tell you that you were giving a statement on the basis of a request from the Association of Detainees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I gave the statement for the court and they then forwarded the statement to the Association of Detainees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who informed you about the fact that that statement would be forwarded to the Association of Detainees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nobody told me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that that statement was forwarded to this Association?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure about that, but when I saw it here, I think now that the Association had sent it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this morning when you were answering the questions asked by my colleague, you were not giving the entire fact that you had known, so you were not speaking the whole truth?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I object to that question being put, your Honour. It is not a question of not speaking the whole truth. It may be a question of not giving the full details of what he could say about the matter. That is not necessarily not speaking the whole truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually the witness has not said that he was sure it was being sent to them. He assumed it was being sent to them. That does not mean it was being sent to them, to the Association of Detainees. He assumed that the court was sending it to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, but when asked by colleague Ackerman, the witness said precisely that in Visegrad he gave the statement for the Association of Detainees. That is why I asked additional questions, and the clarification from the witness is either a clarification or a different presentation, a different account. I would not be going back to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: -- that he made a statement to the Association of Detainees. He was summoned to the court where he made a statement, and the question was, "How did they know?" He said he received a summons and went to the court and made this statement. To your question about how the statement got to the Association of Detainees, he said he was not too sure, but he assumed it was sent to them. I do not see much of a discrepancy in the questions. The questions were answered in the order in which they were framed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I do apologise if that is the case, because I firmly believed that I had heard the witness, but I do accept that it is as you said, your Honour, in the transcript it is certainly recorded. Thank you very much for your warning. I do apologise if I interpreted what the witness said differently. However, Mr. Kuljanin, the first sentence of your statement given before the judge in Visegrad is the following: "In early June 1992 I was in the Serb village of Cerici near Konjic when the Muslim armed forces attacked this village on 10th June 1992, and on that occasion I was taken prisoner together with Miro Golubovic from Cerici." Did you say this to the investigative judge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told the investigating judge that the attack took place on the 10th and that I was not arrested then, but 20 maybe days later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said to the investigators that you and Miro Golubovic surrendered to Darko Verkic on 9th June; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I asked you, you responded that the fighting in Donje Selo took place between 20th and 23rd May. Are those totally different events?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot really determine the day. It was five years ago. Whether it was the 8th or the 9th that I was brought there, I am not sure, but I think it was more possible that it was the 8th when I was brought to Celebici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the statement given to the investigative judge, it says that the attack took place on 10th June.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said around 10th June, I think it was on about that date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have just responded to me --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was 20th to 23rd --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You got me confused, the attack was in May and I surrendered on the 7th, 8th or 9th. It was in 1992, June, so 15 or 20 days later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if in the statement of the investigative judge given in Visegrad it says that the attack against Donje Selo and Cerici was 10th June and on the same day you were taken prisoner, that is not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is not true, but it was interpreted wrongly. I said that I had surrendered on the 10th and that the attack was on 20th or 25th, but it was in May. Since I was in hiding for about 15 days after that, in the woods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is a statement which you read and for which you said before this court that it did not contain any incorrect information; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it is not a very big mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would just like to consult my documents, your Honours. (Pause). Just a question I did not understand clearly. Drasko Dragovic, you gave an automatic rifle to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not give him a rifle, he had a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, your Honour. I think I am about to finish my part of the cross-examination. I would just like to look into another thing. Could you please confirm for us that I have an Ivica Azinovic, President of HVO Konjic, was there at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any other cross-examination? Cross-examined by MR. OLUJIC

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With your permission, your Honours. Good day, Mr. Kuljanin. My name is Zeljko Olujic, I am an attorney from Zagreb, I am Defence counsel for Mr. Zdravko Mucic. You have mentioned him during the examination-in-chief and the cross-examination. I would like this conversation between the two of us to be carried out in a technically appropriate manner and that means, since we speak languages that we both understand, I speak Croatian and you speak Serbian, we have to wait for the interpretation into both English and French so as to avoid the appearance that we are conducting a dialogue and to allow the Trial Chamber and all of us in the courtroom, both on the Prosecution side and the Defence side, so that they can follow the cross-examination. Are we in agreement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, I am sorry to hear that you have been in The Hague for a week. This has taken rather long, so I will try to cut down my questions to a minimum and I ask for your patience so that you are able to go back to your home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, you said that you had done your national service and I mean JNA, from the former State, that you did national service in 1990 and 1991, or 1991 to 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went in June 1990 and I returned in June 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that you went to the reserve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you spend in the reserve forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A month and a half or two, I do not know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a rank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which branch of the army were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Infantry, rear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, you described when you were arrested -- you described in detail the circumstances of the arrest itself. I would like to know, did the persons wear uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they wore camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These persons, did they address each other using ranks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not notice that, just names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came to Celebici, did the guards have uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In different clothing, camouflage trousers and just T shirts as tops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we then say that this was not a proper uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the guards, did they use ranks when addressing each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, just first names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the camp itself, was there a lack of discipline among the guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the guards punished for lack of discipline?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see that, maybe yes, maybe there was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the examination-in-chief, Mr. Kuljanin, you mentioned that you would have been killed if it had not been for Zdravko Mucic who transferred you to the infirmary.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that by doing so, Mr. Mucic acted in a humane manner by transferring you there and saving your life?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said during the examination-in-chief that you were physically abused and it was really hard to listen to all that you have been through. It is not easy. But I would like to ask you to answer just one more question. In addition to the physical abuse that you were subjected to, during the examination-in-chief you mentioned that you were also abused by other passers-by; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, passers-by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you, Mr. Kuljanin who were those persons, those passers-by, who did you mean when you used that term?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were members of different units from Sarajevo to Mostar, those small groups, intervention units, people whom I had not seen before in my life, nor did I know their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean, Mr. Kuljanin, that in addition to the guards who were in the camp, that other military units also passed through the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those various units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they obey the commands of the gentlemen who were in the camp or did they act whichever way they wanted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They acted in their own way, they acted as they wanted to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kuljanin, can you dismantle a rifle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you fire a rifle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you do that quickly? Are you able to dismantle and reassemble a rifle very quickly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, I have not tried it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many bullets, rounds are there in a Kalashnikov?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 30. That was the weapon I signed out in the army. I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. (Pause). Well, that will be all, Mr. Kuljanin. I wish you a pleasant trip.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour it always seems to take a while to get wired up over here for some reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It makes it easier for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much for the time, your Honour. May it please the court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Go on. Cross-examined by MR. MORAN

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Kuljanin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My name is Tom Moran and I represent Hazim Delic in this case. The first thing I would like to ask you is you have had a long day today and I understand that. If for any reason you feel tired or fatigued or if you need a drink of water or to take a break, you let me know and we will see if we can arrange it, okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I am concerned, we can continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Great. But if we come to a point where you are feeling fatigued or you just need to sit back for a minute, let me know and we will see if we can get you a break. Like all the other lawyers that have talked to you, I would like you to agree to listen to my questions and answer the question that is asked. It sometimes requires a yes or no, but sometimes might require some explanation. Can you do that for me, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Like all lawyers, sometimes I do not ask the clearest questions in the world, and if I ask a question that you do not understand, nobody is trying to confuse you here, so if you are confused, please stop me and we will work out the question so you understand what I am looking for. Can you do that for me, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, that is great. One other thing, you have been real good about this so far, but it is just my habit to point it out, sometimes you nod, there is two ladies in the courtroom, one over here and one over there who are what are called court reporters. They have to write down everything we say. They cannot write down a nod. We have to sometimes think --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just have to listen? It is a habit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand, sir. No one is trying to press you on that, it is just that sometimes we forget that these court reporters are there. The first thing I would like to ask you is this, sir: I understand you were examined by a physician five days ago; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was that examination?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here in the hospital in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Prosecutor arranged for that examination; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I requested that because I was in considerable pain and the Prosecution allowed me to go to a hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are feeling better now, sir? You are feeling all right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is not bad. It is better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Are you taking any medication right now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Were you taking any medication yesterday, perhaps pain killers or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified earlier today that that man who was with you, Dr. Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He is your personal physician, and sir, I am not asking you what your diagnosis is and I am not asking you to tell me anything that would be what you would consider to be an invasion of your privacy, I am just going to ask you one question that just requires a yes or no. Does any of your treatment with this physician have anything to do with any kind of disease, defect, whatever, that would interfere with your ability to recall events that occurred in the past or to recount those events?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. That is a fair answer, sir. That was all I was asking for. By the way, does he have anything to do with Mr. Draganic, do you know, Rajko Draganic that was here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So when you were all together last night, that was pure happenstance, I take it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, fair enough. By the way, did you talk to anybody over lunch about this case, perhaps Mr. Niemann or one of the investigators from the Office of the Prosecutor or Dr. Jovanovic or anybody like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we only had lunch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Dr. Jovanovic, by the way, is a member of the Association of Detainees, is he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he is a member.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You became his patient -- did the association refer you to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the association sent him here with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. He's been your treating physician for some time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I do not think he understood your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. Let me try and -- I think you might have misunderstood the question. Judge Karibi-Whyte thinks so. Let me try it again and see if we can get it straight. When you initially went to Dr. Jovanovic, presumably you did not know him before you became his patient and he did not know you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did know him before you became his patient?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it the Association that suggested that you go to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Association sent him as my escort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, but before you came here, what I am trying to ask, sir, is this: the very first time you became his patient back in however many months ago it was that you started seeing him for treatment, was it the Association of Detainees that recommended that -- said "Dr. Jovanovic is a good guy, go see him", that kind of thing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Is it not more "how did he become his doctor?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise, but this doctor is a doctor with the Association. Dr. Jovanovic is with the Association, just like Dr. Bjelica is a doctor with the Association. They work for the Association.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay, that is fine. That was all I was trying to get at, sir. Do you know, sir, if there was any reason why he would have been here yesterday to watch Mr. Draganic's testimony? He is not his escort, is he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Something else and if you think that -- again if you think I am getting into a matter that invades your privacy, let me know and I will either withdraw the question or go into private session so no one outside the court can hear it. Let me just preface my question with this: I have been informed by the Victims and Witnesses Unit of the Tribunal that as a general rule they do not pay for or authorise people to pay for, or they will not reimburse an escort for someone to come to The Hague to testify, and that the general rule is that they have escorts authorised for people that are ill, infirm, maybe somebody that is elderly and cannot get around. What I am getting at is there has to be a good reason for it. Do you know why the Victims and Witnesses Unit authorised you to have an escort, if in fact they did?
