utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was due to my condition, the condition I am in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the interests of not invading the man's privacy any more, I am going to change the subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: If the court wishes me to follow up, I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If it is your case, but as much as possible, you avoid questions which might be undesirable unless you really need it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Again in the interests of this witness's privacy I think we can go on to something else. Let me go to the time when you immediately got to Celebici. As I recall your testimony, and I think you just testified to it again a couple of minutes ago, as soon as you got to Celebici, a Muslim policeman, you have no idea who it was, attacked you with a knife while you were still in the car; do I have your testimony right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, while we were sitting there in the car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there a whole lot of soldiers around the entrance at the time you got there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, all told there were maybe 15 or 20 of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they look like they were -- sir, you were in the JNA and the JNA was a fairly disciplined army.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know what a disciplined army was or is. Did these guys look disciplined, or were they out of control?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The people who were there when I got there, I think they were out of control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this man attacked you with a knife, you said Mr. Delic, and who else hustled you away from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, after five minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they protected you from -- I presume you were scared when this guy came at you with a knife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I was surprised, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I presume you thought that the guy --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was drunk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you had a drunk with a knife that was coming at you to attack you, and Mr. Delic got you away from that, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the manhole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is right. He got you to some place where that man with a knife could not get at you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he took me to the manhole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is true. Nobody is denying that. He got you to a place --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just wanted to tell you where he brought me to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He brought you to the manhole and he put you down the manhole, no question about it. What I am suggesting to you, sir, is that while you were in that manhole, that undisciplined mob of people, including the drunk policeman with a knife, were unable to harm you; is that a fair assessment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they could not get into the manhole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is right, so they could not harm you; is that fair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I just do not know who had the key, whoever had the key was the person who protected us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that when you were released from the manhole, what a day and a night and a day later, right, so about 24 to 36 hours later, is that about how long you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were released from that manhole, was that drunken mob of undisciplined people with knives and guns still around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were not there right next to the manhole, but they were still there. There were a few of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they look like they were under a little bit more control, a little bit more disciplined?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It did not look to me like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, you have talked to everybody up here about the statements, the previous statements you have made. I do not want to beat a dead horse, but I am afraid I will have to do it a little bit. I know you are tired of hearing about this, but I would like to talk about a couple of things. The first thing is, when you met with Mr. Niemann --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think we should break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: At 4.30 you can start with that topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will beat that dead horse when we return. (4.00 pm) (A short break) (4.30 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Moran, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, before he begins, may I make a request to the court? After today, there will be nothing before the Trial Chamber tomorrow or Friday that has any impact on Mr. Landzo. He has asked that he be excused from attendance on Thursday and Friday. Ms. McMurrey and I have no objection to that if the court has no objection to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I suppose before we close today we will tell you what the decision is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. I wanted to mention it now, because I was afraid I would forget it by 5.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, so I do not forget it, Mr. Delic is in the same position and asks to be excused also. In any case, may it please the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: One witness is on his way to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is correct, your Honour. There is a witness coming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You are expecting a witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: There is one on his way, but he will not be arriving until late tonight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think this complicates the matter. Since we are expecting a witness who is likely to come, it is important we take that witness, if he arrives.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I understand, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: So tomorrow, perhaps they have to wait until we know what the position is tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was aware that there is another witness coming. It is my understanding that that witness has absolutely nothing to say about Mr. Landzo, has no idea who he is or anything else and is not being called as a witness against Mr. Landzo. That is the reason I made the request the way I did. I was aware of the witness at the time I made the request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I suppose it might still be difficult for the Trial Chamber to decide that nothing will affect him from the evidence. You never can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That is fine, your Honour. Thank you very much for the consideration on that. Good afternoon again, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you this about one of your statements and I am not going to show it to you, but remember when you were meeting with Mr. Niemann, the Prosecutor, those three times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He went over the statement that you gave Sabina Manke back in February 1996 with you, went over it in great detail, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, one could say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spent, what, about three or four hours going over it, so that is pretty good detail.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I object to that, your Honour. That is not what the witness said. The witness said it was for an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I am sorry, an hour and a half going over it, so in fairly good detail?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It all --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I am getting it, sir, is this: having read my statement yourself and having listened to your testimony, there were several places in your statement where, for whatever reason, there was a mix-up between a man named Osman Dedic and Hazim Delic. Do you recall some of those incidents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was their mistake, not mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. No one is saying you did anything wrong, sir. No one is criticising you at all, okay? What I am asking you is this: was Mr. Niemann aware of those problems with your statement when he talked to you in private?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to that. I am not sure how the witness would know what I was aware of and what my problems were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, let me rephrase this. Did you make Mr. Niemann aware of the problems in the statement where Mr. Dedic and Mr. Delic had their identities confused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know the difference between Osman Dedic and Hazim Delic very well. Perhaps Mr. Niemann ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps he did not understand the difference or perhaps it was not clear to him, is that what you are saying, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I do not know what you have in mind. Is it not the evidence that determines where either of them comes in? One is a guard and the other is not a guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That is correct, your Honour. In fact, I am not going to tender the statement. I was just bringing before the court that there was some confusion over the names, for instance, there was an incident yesterday afternoon right before the afternoon break where the last question was something, the answer was Osman Dedic was involved in a beating and the first question after the break was "Mr. Delic ..." And then the witness quite properly corrected the questioner. I just wanted to make clear to everyone that that had occurred. Sir, that was not the first time that you had a chance to go over that statement that you gave Ms. Manke, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have gone through it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You went through it with her back in November 14th last year, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And had the chance to make any corrections you wanted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I did that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, you made some corrections in some other statements. According to your statement, and I will be happy to provide you with a Bosnian Serbian translation of it, that you were shown the statements that were given to the Bosnian authorities on 7th February 1994 and to the authorities in Visegrad, that would have been the Serbian court, on 3rd February 1995, which actually was 1996, and you made, I believe --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- two changes to those statements and one paragraph or two paragraphs clarifying things. Is that a fair assessment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what the question is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Perhaps with a little help from the usher, if we could mark this as Delic exhibit whatever, whatever our next one is.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is D11/3.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay, sir. If you just want to read that it will help you refresh your memory about what you were shown back then. (Pause). Sir, if you take my word for it, that is a Serbian translation that is from the Office of the Prosecutor. I would be glad to show you the original in English with your signature on it, if you would like.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am supposed to say?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am just asking you -- okay. Look at the first paragraph --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a correction that I requested in the statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That he did not tell me -- that it was not Zdravko Mucic who told me to enter the manhole, it was Hazim Delic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. What I am getting at, sir -- you are getting ahead of me here. Let us back off a second. According to this statement, you were shown three statements by Ms. Manke, the statement that you gave to her on February 23rd; the statement that you gave to the Bosnian authorities on February 7th 1994; and the statement you gave in Visegrad to the Serbian investigating magistrate. Is that not what the first paragraph seems to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only received one statement from Ms. Manke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Ms. Manke only showed you one and there were corrections to -- or the possibility --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the Bosnian authorities. I think that was the one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So just the statement that you made on February 7th 1994, that is the only one that you saw; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember the dates when I gave them. Okay, it was extensive perhaps, those were actually two statements, but I understood that to be one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me see if we can help you out. If the usher could show you Prosecution Exhibits 176 and 177? Those should be the Serbian versions of a statement that you gave on February 7th 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, my records indicate that 176 is 15th January 1994. 177 is 7th February, so therefore ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I think he needs to have both of them, Mr. Niemann.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I just thought --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I understand. You are correct though. His records are correct, your Honour. I am just trying to save the usher a trip. When Ms. Manke showed you all these statements back in November of last year, did she show you both of those or just one of them, or do you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The reason I say that is, and maybe you can help me with this, if you go to the statement that you gave her, that one page statement I handed you a little while ago, the very first statement I handed you, D11/3, if you go down to the second paragraph, it says that you want to make a correction in your statement of February 7th to page 1, paragraph 2, where you say it should read, and then if you look at Prosecution Exhibit 177, it fits, the correction you want to make fits. You have what the statement should be. Do you want to take a look at those two and compare them and see if that is fair?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Is it your question that he has corrected the statement of 7th February?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to get right to the heart of the matter, the next paragraph which does not mention anything at all about the 15th January statement, contains a correction to the 15th January statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: This one refers to 7th February.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: So what he is supposed to have corrected is that statement of 7th February.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, and the next statement which in his November 14th statement to the OTP, the next paragraph is quoted at length, a sentence from it, and in fact that sentence is not in Prosecution Exhibit 177, the 7th February statement, it is in the 15th January statement, which would seem to indicate that he has had access to more than just those three statements that were here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I assume a progressive correction has been made to each of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. The point is that he did have the chance to correct any of these statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The January one and the February statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: At least those two. I want to find out how many more of these he had a chance to correct. Sir, will you take my word for it, so we can save ourselves a lot of time, that if you look at your statement to Ms. Manke from November of last year, it contains corrections to two different statements you gave to the Bosnia authorities, one which is Prosecution Exhibit 176, a January 15th statement, and the other which is Prosecution Exhibit 177, a February 7th statement? Will you take my word for that? If not, I will be happy to go through it with you. If it would help the Prosecution, they seem to be looking for it, your Honour, the paragraph that is corrected in the 15th January statement is the last paragraph of the first page , starts off "Verkic joined in the meantime by Pavo Mucic". It reads directly into the correction in the OTP statement. Sir, would you agree with me that you have probably had access to more than one of the statements you gave the Bosnian authorities when you talked to Ms. Manke back in February -- excuse me, back in November of last year? It appears that that is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that I had made a correction in that and I said exactly what happened, the statements taken by the Bosnian authorities for me are not of any significance, because they deliberately missed out the names. Instead of Hazim Delic, they put the name of Pavo Mucic, Zdravko. That was not an accident, that was done deliberately.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, just in relation to the statement of 15th January 1994, what I have in the statement that I have is "Verkic who had been joined by Pavo Mucic, the commander of the prison, in the meantime ordered us to get out of the car and go down into the manhole", which is in some ways quite different to the other one. There are similarities, but it is not precisely the same. Just to draw that to counsel's attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I suppose, is that not what is being corrected when Ms. Manke went over it with him?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Actually, your Honour, what I think occurred is the statement to Ms. Manke says "here is the sentence which needs to be corrected" and, therefore, admittedly a couple of minor differences in the wording, I think they have to do with translation and stylistic matters, as opposed to substance. Substantially they are the same sentence. I would be happy to introduce my one copy of the English version of November 14th --

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That might be so, your Honour, but I do not think you can say that one is identical with the other therefore it is obviously the statement of the 15th. The point I make is that it is not identical. In other words, there may be a similar sense to it, it may be speaking of the same topic and, indeed, it may be covering the same point, but you cannot say one is identical with the other when they are not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I thought counsel was trying to reflect on the fact that the November exercise was intended to correct certain things in January and February.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I think the point, as I understand it he is saying that the statement that was corrected was, in fact, the statement of 15th January 1994, and he says that is so because he says there are paragraphs -- the paragraph is the same. The point I make is that the paragraph is not the same. It is about the same topic, I agree with that, but the words are not exactly the same. He cannot say for sure that that is what this statement is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What does the correction read, because that might help?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will read the whole thing to the court, or we can put it on the ELMO so everyone can see it. Whatever makes the court happy. I am flexible on this. The statement given to Ms. Manke last November, the paragraph reads: "In my statement to the BH authorities, page 1, paragraph 4, sentence 1, the facts are not correctly laid down: 'Verkic meanwhile joined by Pavo Mucic, the commander of the prison, ordered us to get out of the car and go town into the tank.' "Pavo Mucic did not order me to get out of the car and go into the tank, I only heard his voice later when Verkic and Delic had already put me in the manhole. Verkic is the driver I am referring to in my statement to the ICTY." Your Honour, if you go to paragraph 4, sentence 1 of the statement dated 15th January 1994, which is Prosecution Exhibit 176, it reads: "Verkic, joined in the meantime by Pavo Mucic the commander of the prison" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would counsel please slow down a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Let me start over: "Verkic, joined in the meantime by Pavo Mucic, the commander of the prison, ordered us to get out of the van and into the manhole." Your Honour, I submit that given the stylistic changes in translation from English to Serbian and Serbian to English, that that is the same sentence that is referred to in his statement to Ms. Manke.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but it is not the same person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Clearly, and you were allowed to make any corrections you wanted to in those statements that you made to the Bosnian authorities, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Never. How can I make corrections?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you met with Ms. Manke back last November she gave you the chance to make corrections. You made at least two, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And I did correct it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sure. Anything that was wrong with those statements you fixed, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember that exact moment very well when it comes to the entry into the manhole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sure. When you went over those statements --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Excuse me, but how can she make corrections of statements she did not take?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, what she did was -- from reading her statement and this is reading between the lines, he was given a chance to add and/or clarify those statements, which is the words out of his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Statements made to some other authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. The Office of the Prosecutor provided him with at least one of these statements, according to the witness statement that he gave to Ms. Manke, or in some way, shape or form, he was given a chance by Ms. Manke in a statement taken by the OTP in November of last year to add to, clarify, correct clearly the statement of 7th February, which is Prosecution 177, I submit Prosecution 176, and also the statement made to the investigating magistrate in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, might I raise a matter at this stage? As I pointed out previously, if counsel reads the second paragraph of the statement, rather than reading between the lines, one can see what is there. It says: "I did not believe that I could add the entire and complete truth to the statements that I gave to the Bosnian authorities." That is completely contrary to what counsel is asserting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I am saying that he says in his statement, the very first paragraph: "I would like to add and to clarify the following:"

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Exactly right, your Honour and specifies what the following are. Counsel is reading into this statement more than is there. He is trying to suggest that a complete revision of the statement was done, it was not. There were a couple of issues that wanted to be clarified and that was done. He says in the second paragraph: "I did not believe that I could add the entire and complete truth to the statements that I gave to the Bosnian authorities." In my submission that makes the whole issue quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, our position is that he had a chance to change whatever he wanted to. The Prosecution said "here, tell us what is wrong with it".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Do you not think that is strange? It was not a statement made to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Actually, your Honour, if I were the Prosecutor and I had a statement that was given to -- you knew you were going to have to give in discovery and I knew that there were some factual errors in that statement, I would try and get something to correct that statement with factual errors in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The statement he made to someone else?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: The statement he made to whoever, but in any case, your Honour, we can go on to another subject. Sir, I am a little confused about something, I think the record is not real clear and I would like to see if you could maybe help me with this. That statement that you gave in Visegrad to the investigating magistrate, okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was done at the behest of either the document centre or the Association of Detainees, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I was summoned to the court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me tell you, sir, why I wanted to probe into that a little bit. This morning, the transcript, and it is the LiveNote's transcript, starting at page 17, line 25, if the Prosecution wants to check my reading, you have question by Mr. Niemann: "Do you remember the circumstances of the document being created?" Do you remember him asking that question, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember your answer to that, because I can help you with it. I have it off the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I said the same thing that I said a minute ago, that I had been summoned to give a statement, that I had received a summons from the court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Actually, what the transcript taken down by that court reporter says is: "Answer: yes. I was invited by the investigators from the documentation centre and the Association of Detainees in Belgrade and that is this statement. I gave this statement in the court building of the Visegrad municipality." Do you remember that being your answer, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I am just explaining to you how I came to be at the court. I received a summons to appear before the court. I do not know who told them to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you were answering Mr. Niemann's question this morning, did you not understand the question, when you talked about the Association of Detainees and the documentation centre, or was that just a slip of the tongue: what was it, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember I said that I thought that it was at the request of the Association of Detainees, that that was how it came to be that I gave this statement to the court. I did not say that they sought that statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You can now link the answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The answer is -- sir, did this -- I do not think the record is still real clear. I would like to just clarify it just a bit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is fine with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This morning, reading that answer that I just read to you, it seems to me that you thought you were giving, or at least you were telling Mr. Niemann and you wanted the judges to believe that you were giving -- you were invited by the investigators from the documentation centre and the Association to give a statement and then --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me just a second. Then you say that the reason you went there was because you got this summons from the court. You are not telling anybody that that summons just kind of came out of the blue, are you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this is the procedure that has to be followed. This is the court's procedure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, we will all agree that the Association of Detainees and the documentation centre arranged for you to get that summons, right, in all likelihood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that is how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, fine. I just wanted to clear that up, sir. One last thing and then I will be done, okay? Or I think I will be done. You can never trust lawyers on that kind of thing. Do you remember that tape that Ms. Residovic showed you a little while ago, that tape of you making that statement? It is defendants' 68/1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course. I will remember it for as long as I live.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Remember how you said that we could not see the desk and that you were reading a statement that was on the desk, do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The desk was to my right, to my side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, so the desk was off on your side and you were reading the statement that was on that desk off to your side; is that right? On your right side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and it was written by -- I do not know who it was, what her name was. In fact they were prompting me what to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the statement was laying down on the desk off to your right; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The statement was this format, and they would write something with a pencil and tell me, "read it out" and then I would read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. That is that videotape defendants' 68/1. Judge, with the permission of the court I would like to re-show that tape. I do not care if there is any audio with it, I do not care if there is any translation with it, I just want to show the court the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You want to repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Just the video. We do not need any translation or audio. If the court wants it, the court is welcome to it. I do not think that is necessary for what I want to show it for. I want the witness to see it as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Please let us have the video played.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: While you are watching this, sir, I would like you to -- when you see yourself looking down and to the right to read that statement, just say stop and we will have them stop the tape for you. Can you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If they play the audio, if you would say stop when we can hear the people telling you what to say.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they should just show a picture of the whole room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, unfortunately we do not have a picture of the whole room, we only have what is on this videotape?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: How would you see anybody at the background prompting him?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I asked him to stop it when he heard somebody telling me. That should be on the audio. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am familiar with the statement, but you should show the room where I was, so that I can show you where it was. Stop, please. (Videotape stopped)

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: If we back it up just a tad, that is where you look down and to the right to see the statement that was written for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you show the desk where I was sitting, the desk that was in front of me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I want to see where you look down and to the right, where you describe that statement was. We can fast forward it, we do not need to hear it. Unfortunately I do not have the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand what you are saying, but you do not understand me either. I want to tell you that there is a tape of the desk where I was sitting and of the chair where I sat and there was a paper on the desk, and on this paper there were the words that I was supposed to read. You could see me on that tape reading.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I am afraid I do not have that tape and that tape is not in evidence, but I would submit to you at least until this point of the tape, I will show you the rest of it if you would like, I have not seen you look down and to the right yet, and yet you testified earlier that the document that you were reading from and people were writing and prompting you to say those words, was off on your right on a desk to your right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a bed where Hazim Delic slept, there was a desk and they sat next to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And they sat off to your right and you were looking -- your Honour, let me make one quick look through my notes. Your Honour, while I am looking through my notes, can we play the rest of the tape? It is just a couple more seconds, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Let us have the tape and see whether it will corroborate. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stop. Here you can see me look to the side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Back off, if we could. So that is looking down and to your right, okay sir. We can run the rest of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, might I raise a matter? (Videotape stopped)

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Could the tape be taken back to the point where it was when it commenced. It is very clear that he appears to be looking at something and it is not that section. I would ask that it be taken back for counsel to see. This is the part here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Let it run. Let us just run the whole thing through. Whatever makes the court happy makes me happy, judge. We can start at that point and just run it through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Let us have the tape from the beginning and see how that fits in. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You still think we need to watch this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, whatever makes the court happy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is not the court's evidence, it is the parties. You know why you want this tape. I think it has nothing to do with the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Then stop, unless Mr. Niemann wants to show it later or something, I am done with it. (Videotape stopped)

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am happy for the moment, your Honour. I just did not want to have to laboriously go through it again in total in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: One last thing, sir. Remember probably in July or August 1992 at the camp, when it became possible for people's relatives to visit them, their wives, their mothers, their sisters and leave them food and clothing and things like that, do you remember that, some time in July or August 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometimes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As I understand it, the people that were in your family for some reason were not able to get you that food and clothing and things like that; is that a pretty fair assessment of the situation? Maybe they were not around or for whatever reason.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not have any relatives in Konjic and that was fortunate for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it not true that because you were one of the few people that was not given packages by your relatives that Mr. Delic would give you cigarettes in the evenings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It happened twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much, your Honour. Pass the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Is there any re-examination? Re-examined by MR. NIEMANN

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kuljanin, just going back to the tape that you were shown a moment ago, when I saw the tape I counted at least four occasions when you appeared to be looking on the screen to the right of the screen, presumably it would have been to your left when you were sitting there. Are they the occasions that you were reading from the script that had been written for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When this script -- did you know who wrote the script?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I just received some general outline of what I was supposed to talk about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was in the room at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember those people. I do not know them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anyone armed or did anyone have any weapons or implements in their possession at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can just remember very well that maybe half an hour or an hour before that I was beaten so badly that I could hardly sit on the chair and when I got into that room, nothing happened, but all along the corridor and in front of building number 22, that is where it happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of the people that beat you in that room at the same time as you were required to read that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Hazim Delic entered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have anything in his hands at the time when he was in the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember. He was behind my back. He passed by my side. He had a pistol in his belt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you asked whether or not you agreed with the contents of the statement that you read out on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No way, by no means.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that just prior to being taken into the room you had been beaten. On what part of the body had you been beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On my back and on my legs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were being cross-examined by Madam Residovic, you made reference to a sniper rifle. Was this a military sniper rifle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I think I was quite clear that it was a small calibre rifle that is used only for sports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it a rifle that was fitted with telescopic sights?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said when you left the JNA barracks at Mostar you took with you two bombs. Do you mean hand grenades?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hand grenades.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again in response to a question by Madam Residovic, you referred to the person driving the IVECO van and there is some uncertainty in the transcript as to who this person was and the position that that person had at the time. Can you just tell us who it was that was driving the IVECO van and what position that person had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was the driver, he was the driver for the entire camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know his name? If you do not know his name, it is okay. If you did know, perhaps you could tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I think his last name was Buric. I do not know what his first name was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Moran suggested to you that you were put in the manhole to be taken out of harm's way because of the drunk that attempted to stab you. Do you think from what you could observe at the time whether it may have been possible to put the drunk in the manhole?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour. This calls for pure speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If my friend was not suggesting that you were not put in the manhole for that purpose then I will withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If all you were correcting was that he felt that was the way to protect him, I think that is all he answered. He should be able to know whether that was the purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you think you were put in the manhole for the purposes of being protected from the drunk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think so, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I have no further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, in view of Mr. Niemann's re-exam, I know it is not ordinarily appropriate to do this and this may be the only time I will request it in this trial, it probably is, but because there is a matter before the court that I think is unclear, I would like to ask leave of the court to ask this witness an additional question by way of demonstration basically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Did it arise out of re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It arose out of the re-examination based upon whether or not this witness during the videotape was reading a statement. I think I need to ask an additional question about that just to try to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I do not know. You were the person who introduced that video?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I was not. It is a matter of concern to all of us, of course, but I was not the one who introduced it. I am in your Honour's hands. I am making the request --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I am merely saying in terms of procedure whether in fact it is one of your own questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: In terms of procedure I may not be the proper person to be doing it, but I am the one that is prepared to do it at this point. If I could have a conference with one of my colleagues, maybe the person who asked the person would be prepared to do it, or maybe it is not appropriate to do it at all, but I think it is and I think it would help the Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If you are still in doubt in the area, perhaps one -- you can put the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour could I ask the assistance of the usher to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You have to be aware of one thing. The witness has indicated that for everything to be clear, the whole room ought to be shown, so the table where he is sitting might be visible, but the handicap with which we were watching, makes it difficult to get the whole picture. We will still have you put your question and let us see whether we can clarify the doubts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Judge, I think maybe the matter is as clear as it is going to get. I will abandon my effort. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Because I know the limitations within which you will be asking the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, would you allow me to ask a question that has to do with the cross-examination, because I feel that after that we have still not cleared this matter, and since that re-examination was based on my cross-examination, the answers given now casts an entirely different light and has given an entirely different meaning to what was said, so if I could just ask one more question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I do not know about the ambiguity you are referring to which arises from the re-examination. What is that question?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will tell you immediately. I asked the witness, I actually presented to the witness a statement given to him by Ms. Sabina Manke on page 2 of the English text of the statement, dated 23rd February, on two occasions he said that Mr. Azinovic was present when he left the manhole and when he was beaten for 40 minutes. The witness confirmed that. In re-examination, Mr. Niemann asked the question regarding

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: this ambiguity I would just like the witness to state whether there is a discrepancy in his statement or whether he spoke about two different persons. It is one person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I do not regard this as a discrepancy. If there is an additional person he might have mentioned him, not that the first person you mentioned was not there. He merely added someone else, that is all. That does not affect your own cross-examination. I think that is all we have for this witness. He can be discharged. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Our schedule for tomorrow is likely to be slightly altered because of the proposal of the Prosecution to start another witness tomorrow, but this is still depending on whether this witness will be coming because I hear the witness is still in the air coming. Apart from that, if we have not this witness tomorrow, then we will continue with our schedule of arguing the motions which we have slated for tomorrow. We have the Prosecution's motion of 8th July regarding the admission of evidence, based on the sample of an accused person, handwriting sample, and I think the other motion is the Delalic motion for final examination of the issue of admissibility of evidence. These are the two motions we thought we would be taking this afternoon. But since we could not finish before now, we hope to take them tomorrow. But again as I said, since we are still expecting this witness, we hope -- we will start with the witness and see how far we go, and I think this is because our two weekly vacation comes on the 15th, and if we do not take this witness, it is likely he will be staying here until we resume, because another Trial Chamber is continuing here, so we hope to take this witness tomorrow and see how far we go. After we have disposed of his evidence, then we can take on these arguments. Because of this eventuality, we think all the accused persons have to be here until we know whether we do not need them. So the Trial Chamber will now rise until tomorrow at 10.00. (5.30 pm) (Court adjourned until 10.00 am the following day)
